t: The Eastern Jin carried on the Jin dynasty at Jiankang (Nanjing) after northern China fell to the Xiongnu-led Han Zhao in 311–316.
Power lay with great aristocratic clans such as the Wang, Huan and Xie, while the emperors were usually weak.
Its era saw Wang Xizhi's calligraphy, Tao Yuanming's poetry and the victory over the Former Qin at the Fei River in 383.
dyk: Contemporaries said that 'the Wang and the Sima share the realm', so great was the power of the Wang clan of Langye at the court of the first Eastern Jin emperor.
ev: Sima Rui takes the imperial title at Jiankang as Emperor Yuan
Huan Wen conquers the Cheng Han state in Sichuan
Wang Xizhi writes his preface at the Orchid Pavilion gathering
Jin forces defeat the Former Qin at the Battle of Fei River
Sun En's Daoist rebellion breaks out in the coastal south
Huan Xuan usurps the throne as emperor of Chu
Liu Yu's army conquers the Later Qin and takes Chang'an
Emperor Gong abdicates to Liu Yu, founder of the Liu Song
